Concise Clinical Note

Consult Summary:
27-year-old man with three days of profuse watery diarrhea, abdominal cramps, and mild nausea/vomiting—likely acute gastroenteritis.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Hourly watery diarrhea for 3 days.  
• Associated symptoms: Crampy mid-lower abdominal pain (intermittent, ~6/10), nausea, one episode of vomiting (worse after milk), feeling febrile (no temperature measured), slightly reduced urine frequency.  
• Pertinent negatives: No blood in stool.  
• Past medical history: Denies chronic illnesses; otherwise fit and well.  
• Medications: Paracetamol (dose/route/frequency not documented); no regular prescriptions.  
• Allergies: No known drug allergies.  
• Family history: Father with stage III colon cancer.  
• Social history: Lives with mother and sister; office job in government (Central London). Smokes socially; alcohol moderate with occasional binges (1–2 ×/month). Brother recently had similar diarrheal illness. Preventive care not discussed.

Examination:
Vitals: not recorded.  
Physical exam: none documented.

Impression:
Acute infectious gastroenteritis with risk of dehydration.

Plan:
• Oral rehydration: Advise OTC Dioralyte; maintain clear fluids.  
• Diet: Start with clear fluids/soft foods (e.g., soup, mashed foods); advance as tolerated.  
• Symptomatic relief: Continue Paracetamol for fever or pain.  
• Lifestyle: Avoid alcohol until recovery.  
• Red flags / follow-up: Contact clinic if no improvement within 48 hours or signs of dehydration develop; may require further investigations.  

Quality checks:
● Missing routine elements: No vitals, weight, or hydration status documented; no stool culture or physical exam.  
● Internal conflicts: None noted.  
● Transcript quality: Clear; occasional conversational overlaps but clinically intelligible.
